### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2becfd615d57500ce554935db934c07c00c09db2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0a70ecc69b3c07f6f89881d6028fdad79f9acde0` — the merge of head `1789606ebfb6e2eab004baf912a1a11ef6cb490f` into base `2becfd615d57500ce554935db934c07c00c09db2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0a70ecc69b3c07f6f89881d6028fdad79f9acde0 && git checkout 0a70ecc69b3c07f6f89881d6028fdad79f9acde0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2becfd615d57500ce554935db934c07c00c09db2 1789606ebfb6e2eab004baf912a1a11ef6cb490f && git checkout -B drift-repro 2becfd615d57500ce554935db934c07c00c09db2 && git merge --no-ff 1789606ebfb6e2eab004baf912a1a11ef6cb490f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2becfd615d57500ce554935db934c07c00c09db2
```

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (L1, first read) · Head-sha: 02e274bd70d55ebdf1bee21f510133aef0c85ab6 · 2026-11-16T17:12Z

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-B, reading the final head declared in 6923403228. I read card #33795, maintainer ruling 6922040858 (letter A: this built half goes ahead as its own `Part of #33795` PR, and "once per recompute, not once per field" on the parent's write path is accepted), the PR body, and the full diff against merge base `80cdbd4e`: 8 files, +588/−24, three commits. The PR is not governed, and the L2 was asked of review#1 in 6923416613.

- **Card relation.** `Part of #33795`, which is right. The batch-end deferral is the second PR, and the open question on it (whether a roll-up a validation rule reads may be deferred) does not touch this half: nothing here moves *when* a recompute runs, only how many statements it costs.
- **One write per parent** (`recomputeSummaries`). The touched parents are collected per descriptor into `writes`, keyed `parentObject|parentId`, so a parent two summary fields point at is written once with both fields. The write is the same engine `update` with `SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE_WRITE`, so a summary over a summary still recomputes up the chain through that update's own recompute (pinned: `a summary over a summary recomputes up the chain`).
- **One aggregate per descriptor.** Values are computed for every parent before the first write, which is sound only while no parent write can move a row an aggregate reads. `reachesChild()` walks the summary graph up from the written parents. When it reaches `childObject` (a self roll-up, or a cycle across objects) the code keeps the per-parent order: aggregate, then write, parent by parent, as before. That is pinned (`a self roll-up keeps per-parent order`). A single parent still asks the one-parent `aggregateSummaryValue`, statement for statement (pinned).
- **The grouped aggregate** (`aggregateSummaryValues`). `where fk $in chunk` ANDed with the descriptor filter, `groupBy: [fkField]`, chunks of 500 ids, so bound parameters stay far below the SQLite and PostgreSQL limits. A parent with no group gets `summaryEmptySetValue`, the same fallback the one-parent path uses. The alias moves to `summary_value` when the FK field is itself named `value`, so `assertAggregatedColumnsAreDistinct` cannot see two columns under one name. Keys are the ids as handed in (`String(id)` on both sides).
- **The record-currency channel (ADR-0144 D6, amended).** I checked whether the roll-up's own aggregate is still admitted when it is grouped across parents. `assertRecordCurrencyAggregatesGrouped` admits a followed amount when `rollupVia === path.via` and does not look at `groupBy`, and `aggregateSummaryValues` always groups by that same `fkField`, so each group is one parent's rows in one currency. The channel rides only when every id in the chunk is concrete, as F3 requires of the one-parent path. `aggregateSummaryValues` is not exported from the package root, so no caller outside the engine can set the channel with a different grouping. By reading, this is correct.
- **Failures.** An aggregate that fails after its retries records one failure for every parent of that descriptor. A write that fails records one failure for every field it carried (pinned: `a failed write reports every field it carried`). The failure list keeps its per-parent, per-field shape, so callers that surface it are unchanged.
- **Pins.**
  - `summary-rollup.test.ts`: the five cases above, on the in-memory double. Three doubles (`engine-summary-recompute-context`, `engine-summary-retry`, `engine-update-prior-read-scope`) were taught `$in`, which only follows the new query shape.
  - `rollup-grouped-recompute-33795.test.ts` (dogfood, SQLite and PostgreSQL): count, sum, min, max, avg, and a filtered count and sum, checked against hand-computed values after a multi-parent `createMany`, an update that moves children between parents, and a delete.
- **Measured** (changeset): `createMany` of 50 rows with 2 summary fields went from 81 to 33 statements, and 50 single-row updates from 550 to 400.
- **Checks on this head** (check-runs): 52 names, 36 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed or running.
- **Base.** PRBASE is `eb0d480b` (Test Core plan), and K = 1. `git merge-tree` against current main is clean.

### Should (before landing, small)

- **S1. Pin the grouped path through a record-currency roll-up.** Every existing record-currency roll-up pin (`record-currency-guards.test.ts`, `record-currency-probes.test.ts`) inserts one line at a time, so it only exercises the one-parent aggregate. If the door ever stopped admitting the grouped shape, a batch write of lines across two invoices would record failures and leave both subtotals stale, and no test would go red. One case in `record-currency-guards.test.ts` covers it: `createMany` of `pp_line` rows across `inv_usd` and `inv_eur`, then each invoice's `subtotal` equals its own lines and no failure is recorded.

### Notes (not blocking)

- **N1.** The docblock on `ROLLUP_AGGREGATE_OPTION` in `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts` (around line 96) still says it is "Set only by `aggregateSummaryValue`". `aggregateSummaryValues` now sets it too, with the grouping that makes it sound. A one-line prose fix when S1 lands.
- **N2.** For the contract reviewer, as the area already flagged: computing every value before the first write widens the window between a parent's aggregate and its write under concurrent child writes. The per-parent loop had the same race, just narrower. Also, a parent update that carries all its fields now succeeds or fails as one unit, which ruling A accepted for the write path.

Landing: not Tier H. Area o1-B lands it after S1 (or a named card for it), the review#1 L2, and green CI.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `1789606ebfb6e2eab004baf912a1a11ef6cb490f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-aggregate.ts + none
Security-touching: no

Area o1-B, the dispatching seat, writes this record on the seat's route (seat note 17:15Z): review#1 declined in 6923461335 because no contract face is touched (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no published schema, no governed path), so the record is TIER_DEFAULT and the dispatching seat writes it with no second agent (contract-review.md). It answers ruling 6922040858 parameter 1, which asks for L1 and a contract review on this half and names the read-to-write window for the reviewer. L1: ACCEPT 6923522845 (first read); fix round 1 (S1 pin, N1 docblock) is on this head, and L1-a reads its delta separately.

### ① Derived judgments

- Values: the grouped aggregate is the one-parent computation over a chunk of ids (`where fk $in chunk` ANDed with the descriptor filter, `groupBy fk`, empty-set fallback kept), so each parent gets the value the per-parent loop gave. A single parent still asks `aggregateSummaryValue`, statement for statement. Pinned on SQLite and PostgreSQL by the dogfood file, and on the record-currency channel by the fix-round pin in `record-currency-guards.test.ts` (two parents, two currencies, one grouped read; ablating the grouped channel reddens it).
- Visible change: a parent carrying N summary fields is written once with all N, so its hooks, validation, audit and realtime run once per recompute instead of N times. Accepted by ruling 6922040858 and stated in the body and changeset.
- Failure shape: an aggregate failure records one failure per parent of the descriptor; a write failure one per field it carried. Unchanged for callers.

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset says. No export, accepted shape or response shape changes. `aggregateSummaryValues` is not exported from the package root.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The read-to-write window (ruling 6922040858 parameter 1).** Today each parent's aggregates are read just before that parent's write, so a parent's window is one aggregate plus one write. The grouped path reads every parent's value first and then writes the parents in order, so the k-th parent's window is k parent writes (each with its hooks and its own recompute up the chain). A batch of 50 rows over 10 parents widens the last parent's window from about 1 write to about 10.
  - What a concurrent write can do in that window: another request's child write lands for parent P and its own recompute writes P's fresh value, and then this batch writes P with the value it read earlier. P's roll-up is stale (it misses the other request's row) until the next child write on P recomputes it from scratch. The same lost update exists on today's per-row path; only its window is shorter. Neither path takes a row lock, and the recompute is a full re-aggregate, never an increment, so a stale value never compounds and the next touch heals it.
  - Does the batch's transaction cover it: the recompute runs in the caller's context (`{ ...execCtx, isSystem: true }`), so it joins a transaction when one is open: inside `engine.transaction(...)`, the cross-object batch, or (by reading `opensAfterAbortUnit`) an `afterInsert` abort unit. On SQLite an open write transaction serialises writers, so the window is closed there. On PostgreSQL at READ COMMITTED the aggregate takes no lock on child rows; the parent update waits for a concurrent holder of P's row and then overwrites, so the lost update is possible in both paths, with the wider window here (by reading, not measured). A plain `createMany` or `updateMany` with no transaction open is covered by none, as today.
  - Within one request, the reading the code guards: a parent write that leads back to the child object through the summary graph (a self roll-up or a cycle) keeps the per-parent order (`reachesChild`, pinned). Not guarded: a parent's own update hook that writes child rows belonging to ANOTHER parent in the same batch. Today that later parent's aggregate would see the hook's rows; here it was read before. A parent hook that writes its own children is fine, since the nested recompute writes after this one. This is rare and heals on the next touch.
  - Judgement: acceptable for this half. The window is wider, not new, and the value self-heals. Nothing here moves WHEN a recompute runs. That question belongs to the deferral half (second PR, its own card thread), whose open validation-rule question this record does not touch. If the maintainer wants the window closed, that is a locking or serialisable-recompute change for its own card, not a fix to this PR.
- SQL push-down: the grouped path pushes one grouped aggregate per chunk of 500 ids down to SQL in place of one aggregate per parent. No new id materialisation beyond the ids the write already holds, and no in-app join.
- Dev flags and open questions: none open. The three test doubles taught `$in` follow the new query shape; no assertion changed.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-33795-rollup-grouped-recompute`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5pHNFS9mn8hS13iGyL`

**VERDICT: PASS**
